<reason>B won a close, high-quality clash by keeping the decision rule on the instrument: cash and respite can recognize care without minting vested contribution years billed to other workers. A’s fairness, existing-credit, and verification-symmetry case was sharp, but the public-savings/supplier claim overreached, two clipped turns hurt completeness, and B’s stoppable-payment versus compounding-credit distinction answered the strongest pressure without conceding the motion.</reason>
